elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 14.3 as rendered retains "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA"; no New York choice of law was inserted. The proposal deliberately targets the fallback level.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: The inserted forum is "exclusively in the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California"; no New York County venue appears.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Retained opening sentence of Section 14.3: "This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of California, USA, excluding conflict of laws provisions..." California is within the accepted set; the clause was left untouched.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 14.3 now reads "Any disputes arising out of this Agreement shall be resolved exclusively in the state and federal courts located in San Francisco County, California, and each party consents to the exclusive jurisdiction of such courts." The mandatory single-arbitrator AAA mechanic is removed, so the forum corresponds to the retained California governing law.

reasons: The finding is correctly classified as a deviation: the original clause paired acceptable California law with mandatory AAA arbitration (single arbitrator, San Francisco seat), which fails the fallback forum element on a material term. The seat was domestic, so this is not walk-away territory, consistent with the rationale.

The fallback checklist is complete as rendered: California law is preserved verbatim and the forum is now the exclusive state and federal courts in San Francisco County, California — the courts corresponding to the retained governing law.

Minimality holds. The governing-law sentence, the conflict-of-laws exclusion and the CISG exclusion are untouched. The deleted sentences (arbitration under the AAA Rules, appointment of one arbitrator, entry of judgment upon the award, and allocation of AAA fees between the parties) are all arbitration-specific machinery that could not operate once arbitration is removed; retaining them would create contradictory or inoperative text, so their removal is necessary rather than cosmetic. No survival tails, fee-shifting substitutes, injunctive carve-outs or other extras were added.

Intent is preserved. The Section 12.2 escrow dispute-escalation cross-reference was conformed ("referred to the courts specified in Section 14.3"), so no dangling reference to a deleted arbitration mechanic remains, and the ten-business-day officer negotiation step, cure periods and escrow triggers survive unchanged. The defined term "RULES" was created and used only within the deleted arbitration sentences, so its removal leaves no undefined term in the operative language.

Non-blocking drafting nit for the drafter: the Section 14.3 caption still reads "Choice of Law; Arbitration; Venue" although no arbitration mechanic remains. This is a non-operative heading and does not defeat the fallback, but conforming it to "Choice of Law; Venue" would remove the stale reference.

Preferred position is not reached and should not be pursued here: New York law and New York County venue would require rewriting the governing-law selection, which the playbook accepts at California; the margin comment correctly states the clause is being brought to the fallback.
